slot.brief: Simplify (1/z̄) or an expression like (1−z)/(1−z̄) using conjugate properties to get a clean form involving modulus.

working:
Given $|z| = 1$, $\bar{z} = \dfrac{1}{z}$. Then $\dfrac{1-z}{1-\bar{z}} = \dfrac{1-z}{1 - \frac{1}{z}} = \dfrac{1-z}{\frac{z-1}{z}} = -z$ (provided $z \neq 1$).

Independent check: Since |z|=1, \bar z=1/z. Thus (1-z)/(1-\bar z)=(1-z)/((z-1)/z)=-z. The denominator is nonzero because z≠1.
solution:
Since $|z|=1$, $\bar z=\dfrac{1}{z}$. Hence
$$\frac{1-z}{1-\bar z}=\frac{1-z}{1-\frac{1}{z}}=\frac{1-z}{\frac{z-1}{z}}=-z,$$
where $z\ne 1$ ensures the denominator is nonzero.
